subject: Fwd: HelioBank security questionnaire escalation - EU data residency guarantees + audit evidence
body:
---------- Forwarded message ---------
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 14, 2025 at 8:22 AM
Subject: HelioBank security questionnaire escalation - EU data residency guarantees + audit evidence

Aisha,

Escalating per HelioBank request. Their CISO is asking for a written guarantee that:
1) all inference processing stays in EU (no cross-region failover),
2) logs/metrics/audit evidence also stay in EU, and
3) we can provide SIEM-ready audit events showing allow/deny decisions.

They’re trying to close security review this week; they asked for an exec (you) to confirm the commitment + what we can put in writing today vs what’s on roadmap/beta.

I attached their questionnaire tab and the exact questions below.

Thanks,
Markus

—
Markus Klein
Solutions Engineering Lead
Redwood Inference


On Tue, Jan 14, 2025 at 7:58 AM Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@heliobank.com> wrote:
> Markus,
>
> We need your CISO to confirm Redwood’s data residency enforcement behavior, not just “we have EU regions.” Specifically, we need assurance that you will not process our prompts/completions outside EU under any failover scenario.
>
> We also require audit evidence for each decision (allowed/denied) and the ability to export it to Splunk.
>
> Please respond in writing and include sample event payloads.
>
> Regards,
> Evelyn
> 
> Evelyn Hart
> Chief Information Security Officer
> HelioBank



From: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>, Sofia Mendes <sofia.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 14, 2025 at 10:41 AM
Subject: Re: HelioBank security questionnaire escalation - EU data residency guarantees + audit evidence

Thanks Markus — pulling in Security Eng + GRC + Legal for a tight answer.

Naomi/Marcus/Olga/Sofia: can we align on what we can state today for Hosted + Dedicated (EU) regarding:
- enforcement semantics (fail closed, gateway admission),
- no cross-region fallback when pinned, and
- audit event fields + export capability.

I’d like to reply to HelioBank by EOD with:
1) clear behavior statement (what is guaranteed, what is configurable)
2) sample audit events
3) what we can contractually commit to now vs beta/GA timeline

Aisha

—
Dr. Aisha Rahman
CISO
Redwood Inference


From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>, Sofia Mendes <sofia.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 14, 2025 at 12:09 PM
Subject: Re: HelioBank security questionnaire escalation - EU data residency guarantees + audit evidence

Here’s the product/behavior summary (Hosted + Dedicated):

What we can state confidently (current beta behavior):
- Region pinning is configured at the org/project level (pinned_region / allowed_regions). If pinned_region is set to an EU region, requests are admitted only in that region.
- Enforcement happens before model execution (at request admission). If a request lands on a non-approved region endpoint or attempts routing to a non-approved region, it is denied.
- When pinned, cross-region fallback is disabled by default. Capacity exhaustion returns an explicit error (vs silently failing over).
- For downstream side effects (audit logs, traces, usage analytics, optional persistence features), the write path is constrained to the same pinned region.

What we need to be careful about:
- “Guarantee” language: we should anchor to “when region pinning is enabled for your org/project, Redwood enforces residency boundaries for in-scope data as described” and keep contract language to Sofia.
- Private deployments: different story (customer-managed), but HelioBank is evaluating Dedicated EU.

GRC/audit:
- We emit audit events for residency policy evaluation and violations. Olga can share retention + evidence notes.

Marcus: can you paste the canonical event schema fields we’re using for the exporter pipeline and any caveats?

Naomi


From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>, Sofia Mendes <sofia.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 14, 2025 at 1:02 PM
Subject: Re: HelioBank security questionnaire escalation - EU data residency guarantees + audit evidence

Event schema details (what we can share externally):

Event types:
- residency.policy_evaluated (emitted for each request at admission)
- residency.violation (emitted when request is denied due to residency)

Common fields we include (high level):
- timestamp (UTC)
- org_id, project_id
- actor_type (api_key | user | service)
- request_id (and optionally trace_id)
- requested_region (derived from endpoint + routing metadata)
- policy (pinned_region and/or allowed_regions, plus policy_version)
- decision (ALLOW | DENY)
- decision_reason_code (e.g., RESIDENCY_REGION_MISMATCH, RESIDENCY_POLICY_MISSING, RESIDENCY_FALLBACK_BLOCKED)
- enforcement_point (gateway_admission | downstream_write)

Export:
- Our audit log exporter supports forwarding these events to customer SIEM. We have sample payloads we can share, and we can explicitly mention Splunk compatibility (HEC) in the response.

Key caveat I suggest we include:
- If a customer intentionally enables a temporary exception (allowing cross-region fallback), the exception is recorded and generates audit entries; otherwise strict mode denies.

I can provide sanitized sample events now.

Marcus


From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>, Sofia Mendes <sofia.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 14, 2025 at 1:37 PM
Subject: Re: HelioBank security questionnaire escalation - EU data residency guarantees + audit evidence

Adding evidence/retention notes suitable for the questionnaire:

- Audit events are retained in accordance with the enterprise audit log retention setting (default 180 days; configurable for enterprise plans).
- We can provide (a) sample payloads, (b) description of event fields, and (c) evidence collection guidance (how to query/export, how to show denial/allow decisions during an audit).
- We can also provide SOC 2 report under NDA separately (not via email attachment).

For wording: avoid “we log prompts/completions in audit logs.” The audit event includes metadata about the decision; it should not contain raw prompt/completion content.

Olga

—
Olga Petrov
GRC & Compliance
Redwood Inference


From: Sofia Mendes <sofia.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 14, 2025 at 2:18 PM
Subject: Re: HelioBank security questionnaire escalation - EU data residency guarantees + audit evidence

Agree with Naomi’s framing.

We can say:
- “When data residency controls are enabled and configured to EU, Redwood enforces processing and in-scope storage/logging within the configured EU region boundary.”

We should not say:
- “We guarantee never under any circumstance…” without tying it to the configured control + product scope.

If HelioBank wants contractual language, I can provide a short addendum clause draft after we confirm their deployment mode (Dedicated EU) and selected region.

Sofia


From: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@heliobank.com>
Cc: Jonas Richter <jonas.richter@heliobank.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 14, 2025 at 5:56 PM
Subject: Re: EU data residency enforcement guarantees + audit evidence (HelioBank)

Evelyn,

Thank you for the clear requirements. I’m Aisha Rahman, CISO at Redwood Inference.

For Hosted API and Dedicated, Redwood supports data residency controls (“region pinning”) that are designed specifically to prevent cross-region processing and to provide audit evidence.

Behavior when EU region pinning is enabled (e.g., pinned_region = eu-west):
1) Enforcement before execution: residency is evaluated at request admission (before model execution). If a request is received in, or would route to, a non-approved region, it is denied.
2) Deterministic routing: when pinned, cross-region fallback is disabled by default. If capacity is unavailable in the pinned EU region, the request fails with a clear residency/availability error rather than silently failing over to another region.
3) Downstream writes: for in-scope operational artifacts (audit logs, traces, usage analytics, and optional persistence features), Redwood constrains the write path to the pinned region boundary.

Audit evidence / SIEM export:
- Redwood emits audit events for residency decisions (allow/deny) and violations. These can be exported to external SIEM tooling (including Splunk). We’ve attached sanitized sample payloads for:
  - residency.policy_evaluated
  - residency.violation

What is included vs excluded:
- The audit events are metadata about the residency decision (org/project, region, decision, reason code, request id/trace id). They do not include raw prompt/completion content.

Next step:
If helpful, we can set up a 30-minute working session this week with your security team to confirm the exact deployment mode (Dedicated EU) + your preferred pinned region and to map the audit events to your Splunk ingestion format.

Regards,
Aisha

Attachments:
- Redwood_Data_Residency_Enforcement_(Beta)_Overview.pdf
- Sample_Audit_Events_-_residency.policy_evaluated_and_residency.violation.json

—
Dr. Aisha Rahman
Chief Information Security Officer
Redwood Inference


From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@heliobank.com>
To: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jonas Richter <jonas.richter@heliobank.com>, procurement@heliobank.com, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jan 16, 2025 at 11:03 AM
Subject: Re: EU data residency enforcement guarantees + audit evidence (HelioBank)

Aisha,

This is helpful. Two follow-ups we need for our risk sign-off:

1) Can you confirm that “denied at admission” means the prompt/completion payload is not processed or persisted outside EU (including transient logging/telemetry)?

2) We need the audit retention period in writing and whether we can configure it to 1 year.

If you can reply today, we can keep our target of completing security review by Monday.

Regards,
Evelyn


From: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@heliobank.com>
Cc: Jonas Richter <jonas.richter@heliobank.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jan 16, 2025 at 7:03 PM
Subject: Re: EU data residency enforcement guarantees + audit evidence (HelioBank)

Evelyn,

1) Yes — “denied at admission” means the request is rejected before model execution. When EU pinning is enabled, Redwood does not route the request for inference execution outside the configured EU region. Our residency audit logging is metadata-only (no raw prompt/completion content), and the audit/log pipelines associated with the residency decision are constrained to the pinned region boundary.

2) Audit retention: enterprise audit logs default to 180 days and can be configured (including 365 days / 1 year) based on your plan and contract terms. Olga Petrov (cc’d) can provide the exact retention option language for your questionnaire and coordinate evidence expectations.

If you’d like, Markus can also share a Splunk mapping example (HEC fields) for the attached sample events.

Regards,
Aisha

—
Dr. Aisha Rahman
CISO
Redwood Inference
